---
name: interface-forge-web
description: Design, build, redesign, and validate distinctive production web interfaces, especially analytical dashboards, admin panels, portals, SaaS products, and landing pages. Use for responsive web UI, data visualization, KPI systems, tables and filters, navigation shells, design systems, light/dark themes, marketing journeys, visual polish, interaction design, accessibility, or browser-based UI quality assurance. Do not use for native-mobile-only products or browser-extension surfaces; use the corresponding Interface Forge specialist.
---

# Interface Forge Web

Build coherent web products with an explicit design thesis, trustworthy data presentation, complete interaction states, and verified responsive behavior. Preserve the project's stack and conventions. Treat starter assets as adaptable foundations, not a required framework.

## Operating contract

1. Inspect repository instructions, routes, components, dependencies, tokens, content, and available tools before choosing an approach.
2. Keep the existing framework and design system unless the user explicitly requests migration.
3. Convert references into principles—hierarchy, density, rhythm, geometry, color behavior, visualization and motion—without copying a protected composition.
4. Build the requested scope completely. Every visible control must work, navigate, change state, or be clearly disabled.
5. Represent loading, empty, error, stale, partial, permission and success states wherever the product can reach them.
6. Verify with the strongest available combination of build checks, browser interaction, screenshots, accessibility checks and performance inspection. Never claim checks that were not run.

## Phase 0 — Route the environment

- Identify the current framework, router, styling system, charting library, state/data layer and testing workflow.
- Inventory capabilities by function: filesystem, shell, preview/browser, screenshot, image input/generation, research and deployment.
- Read [tool routing](references/tool-routing.md) when a capability may be unavailable, paid or permission-gated.
- Read [framework routing](references/framework-routing.md) before introducing a framework or dependency.
- Prefer semantic HTML and platform primitives; add libraries only when they materially reduce risk or complexity.

## Phase 1 — Define the experience

Record the product goal, primary users, decisions the interface supports, required routes, content/data sources, locale and RTL needs, device targets, brand constraints, motion tolerance and acceptance criteria.

Choose the primary product mode:

- **Dashboard/product:** optimize recurring decisions, scanning, filtering, comparison and action.
- **Landing/marketing:** optimize comprehension, trust, differentiation and conversion.
- **Hybrid:** separate product and marketing hierarchies; do not force both into one visual density.

## Phase 2 — Establish a design grammar

Read [style recipes](references/style-recipes.md). Select one recipe or deliberately combine at most two compatible recipes. Read [style packs](references/style-packs.md) when the brief calls for expressive reference-derived directions (aurora focus, neon arena, graphite glass, pastel glass, vivid tiles, playful gradient); apply their brand primitives from `assets/theme-packs.css` via `data-brand` without touching semantic roles. When the brief names a product idea, open [product blueprints](references/product-blueprints.md) first — `assets/blueprints.json` seeds recipe, pack, components, data grammar and first states for fifty common products, and its derivation procedure covers every other idea. State:

1. a one-sentence visual thesis;
2. density, surface, geometry and type behavior;
3. one dominant composition idea;
4. chart/data-ink treatment;
5. motion intensity and reduced-motion behavior;
6. anti-patterns to avoid.

Do not assemble unrelated trends. Glass, gradients, 3D, glow and bento layouts are optional techniques, not proof of quality.

## Phase 3 — Build the theme system

Read [theme system](references/theme-system.md). Implement semantic tokens for light and dark modes, including surfaces, text, borders, actions, status, focus, charts, elevation and overlays. Support system preference, explicit user choice and persistence without a flash of the wrong theme.

Use `assets/theme-system.css`, `assets/theme-controller.js`, `assets/chart-tokens.css`, `assets/focus-manager.js` and `assets/responsive-shell.css` as deterministic references when compatible with the project.

## Phase 4 — Compose from contracts

Read [component contracts](references/component-contracts.md), then inspect `assets/component-contracts.json`. For glow, gradient, glass, ring, tile and loader elements, read [advanced elements](references/advanced-elements.md) and compose from `assets/advanced-ui.css`; adapt community elements (uiverse and similar) only through its hardening checklist. Optional interactive polish (spotlight, tilt, count-up, tab keyboarding, toasts, dialogs with focus return, carousel dots, compare sliders, copy buttons, ticker pause) comes from `assets/ifx-behaviors.js` and must degrade cleanly when absent. When the brief asks for scrolling effects, 3D product motion, exploded views, disassembly or cinematic product pages, read [3D product scrollytelling](references/scrollytelling-3d.md): pick one recipe from `assets/scrollytelling-recipes.json`, drive it with `assets/scroll-scene.js` or GSAP ScrollTrigger, and honor its UX contract (immediate feedback, reversible, landmarks, no scroll hijack, reduced-motion and mobile fallbacks). Treat the catalog as the minimum behavior contract for every selected element: purpose, minimum size, required data, interactions, accessibility, theme behavior and responsive adaptation.

For dashboards, read [dashboard system](references/dashboard-system.md). Establish:

- shell and navigation model;
- information hierarchy and grid spans;
- KPI, comparison and trend strategy;
- chart selection based on the analytical question;
- table/filter/detail relationships;
- refresh, latency, provenance and uncertainty communication;
- saved views, exports and bulk-action behavior when relevant.

For landing pages, read [landing system](references/landing-system.md). Establish the narrative sequence, proof model, primary conversion path, media plan and complete secondary routes before polishing the hero.

## Phase 5 — Implement real behavior

- Use real domain-shaped content; label synthetic/demo data honestly.
- Keep components data-driven and composable rather than generating one monolithic page.
- Provide keyboard, pointer and touch behavior for every control.
- Preserve focus across routing, dialogs and asynchronous updates.
- Use URL state for shareable filters/views where appropriate.
- Reserve media dimensions, lazy-load noncritical content and prevent layout shifts.
- Provide data-table or textual access to chart meaning when a visual alone is insufficient.
- Localize numbers, dates, currency and pluralization; verify realistic expansion and RTL when applicable.

## Phase 6 — Add motion and depth

Read [motion and 3D](references/motion-3d-playbook.md) only when motion improves feedback, hierarchy or storytelling. Use [signature scenes](references/signature-scenes.md) for at most one marketing showpiece. Escalate to [Three.js scroll worlds](references/threejs-scroll-world.md) only for a genuinely spatial narrative.

Preserve native scrolling and task completion. Prefer transform/opacity, pause offscreen work, provide reduced-motion states and fully dispose WebGL resources.

## Phase 7 — Verify

Read [visual QA](references/visual-qa.md). At minimum:

- run build, type, lint and relevant tests;
- inspect 320, 375, 768, 1024 and a wide desktop layout where applicable;
- exercise navigation, filters, tables, forms, menus, dialogs and primary CTAs;
- test keyboard order, focus return, labels, errors, live updates and zoom;
- verify every theme and chart palette, including forced colors and reduced motion;
- inspect loading, empty, error, stale and permission states;
- check console/network failures and performance for heavy media, charts or WebGL.

## Delivery standard

Report what changed, entry points, commands and viewports actually tested, flows exercised, limitations and remaining risks. Deploy only when requested.

## Reference map

| Need | Read |
|---|---|
| Component behavior and catalog contract | `references/component-contracts.md` + `assets/component-contracts.json` |
| Coherent visual directions | `references/style-recipes.md` |
| Reference-derived packs and brand primitives | `references/style-packs.md` + `assets/theme-packs.css` |
| Expressive elements (glow, glass, rings, tiles) | `references/advanced-elements.md` + `assets/advanced-ui.css` |
| Blueprint for any product idea | `references/product-blueprints.md` + `assets/blueprints.json` |
| 3D product scrollytelling and exploded views | `references/scrollytelling-3d.md` + `references/scrollytelling-references.md` + `assets/scrollytelling-recipes.json` + `assets/scroll-scene.js` |
| Light/dark/OLED/high-contrast themes | `references/theme-system.md` |
| Dashboard layout, charts, tables and operations | `references/dashboard-system.md` |
| Landing-page narrative and conversion | `references/landing-system.md` |
| Framework and platform choices | `references/framework-routing.md` |
| Media and icon generation | `references/asset-generation.md` |
| Motion, 3D and signature scenes | `references/motion-3d-playbook.md`, `references/signature-scenes.md`, `references/threejs-scroll-world.md` |
| Browser, responsive, accessibility and performance QA | `references/visual-qa.md` |

references.references/asset-generation.md: # Asset Generation — Cohesive Media Without Vendor Lock-In Use this reference when an interface needs photography, illustration, video, 3D, icons, textures, or social imagery. Route operations through the capabilities available in the current host; never assume a provider or exact tool name. ## Contents 1. Consent and source rules 2. Media DNA 3. Shot-list planning 4. Capability-neutral workflow 5. Embed patterns 6. Icons and exact visuals 7. Fallback ladder 8. Delivery checks ## 1. Consent and source rules 1. Reuse user-provided or repository assets when they are suitable and licensed. 2. Use image search/retrieval for factual or editorial references; record the source and usage constraints. 3. Use generation for original art direction, not for exact charts, diagrams, screenshots, logos, or data. 4. Ask before paid generation, more than three new assets, any video/3D generation, or third-party account usage unless the request already clearly authorizes it. 5. Never send private source material to an external service without authorization. 6. Never embed provider credentials in client code. 7. Do not hotlink fragile search-result URLs. Store permitted assets in the project or use the host's durable asset workflow. ## 2. Media DNA Create one line that every asset shares: `; ; palette , , ; ; ; ; no text or watermark unless explicitly required.` Derive the line from Phase 2 tokens. Keep the subject and composition specific enough that variants remain coherent. | Direction | Useful media language | |---|---| | Trust / enterprise | restrained editorial product photography, clean geometry, soft diffuse light, matte finish | | Developer / security | technical macro detail, high-contrast dark surfaces, one precise luminous accent | | AI / spatial | sculptural abstraction tied to the product metaphor, refractive or tactile material, controlled depth | | Food / wellness | natural light, tactile ingredients/materials, warm shadows, subtle grain | | Luxury / automotive | architectural negative space, single-source light, deep blacks, material detail | | Education / family | friendly shapes, clear silhouettes, bright natural palette, expressive but not childish by default | Avoid generic prompts such as "futuristic AI orb". Name the product metaphor, material, camera position, negative space needed for copy, and exact palette behavior. ## 3. Shot-list planning Generate or source only what the layout needs: | Surface | Asset | Guidance | |---|---|---| | Split hero | one key visual | 4:5 or 1:1; leave copy-side negative space | | Full-bleed hero | one wide image and optional poster | 16:9 or wider crop; protect the focal subject at mobile crops | | Cinematic hero | one short silent loop plus matching poster | motion must loop cleanly and remain optional | | Product showcase | real screenshot or code-native mock surface | never fabricate product claims inside a fake screenshot | | Feature grid | zero to three supporting details | repeat one material/light language | | Testimonials/team | real user assets or clearly fictional consistent portraits | obtain consent for real people | | 3D stage | one optimized model or procedural scene | prefer primitives and simple materials | | Social card | one 1.91:1 composition | reserve readable text area; render text in code when possible | | Empty states | one small icon/illustration family | preserve contrast in light and dark modes | Keep the default media set to eight or fewer assets per page. Art direction and loading discipline matter more than volume. ## 4. Capability-neutral workflow 1. Inspect available media capabilities using [tool routing](tool-routing.md). 2. Decide whether each shot is best retrieved, generated, edited, or built as code. 3. Present the shot list and any cost/account implications when consent is required. 4. Create a small set of variants for the hero, then select one based on composition—not novelty. 5. Create remaining assets with the same Media DNA and consistent aspect ratios. 6. Use edit operations for background removal, crop extension, cleanup, recoloring, or reference-guided changes when supported. 7. Inspect every output at useful detail before embedding it. Check anatomy, text artifacts, logos, repeated objects, crop safety, and palette consistency. 8. Save durable assets into the project or approved asset store with meaningful names. 9. Optimize dimensions and format for the actual render size. 10. Record source/license or generation provenance when the product workflow requires it. If the preferred capability is unavailable, use §7. Do not block the whole UI on optional media. ## 5. Embed patterns ### Responsive hero image ```html ``` Use empty `alt` only when the image is truly decorative and adjacent content already carries the meaning. ### Ambient video with static fallback ```html ``` Start playback only after the element is visible and reduced motion is off. Pause it offscreen, on page hide, and when reduced motion changes. The poster must carry the complete composition. ### Floating cutout without WebGL ```css .cutout-stage { position: relative; perspective: 1000px; } .cutout-stage__glow { position: absolute; inset: 8%; opacity: .35; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 45%, transparent); filter: blur(48px); border-radius: 50%; } .cutout-stage__object { position: relative; width: 100%; height: auto; filter: drop-shadow(0 30px 60px rgb(0 0 0 / .28)); } ``` ### Generated or supplied 3D model Keep the model under the project's asset budget, compress geometry/textures, lazy-load the viewer, cap DPR, pause rendering offscreen, handle context loss, and provide a poster. Prefer a locally installed viewer stack; do not add Three.js solely to rotate a flat image. ## 6. Icons and exact visuals - Use one icon family and consistent stroke/fill geometry. - Prefer existing licensed icon packages already in the project. - Create custom icons as SVG/code when exact shape, states, theming, or accessibility matters. - Use generated raster icons only for illustrative, non-semantic art. - Render charts, maps, diagrams, logos, and interface screenshots with deterministic code or supplied source assets. - Never ask an image model to produce exact legal, financial, medical, or product data. ## 7. Fallback ladder When retrieval/generation is unavailable or inappropriate: 1. Build a token-driven SVG composition with gradients, masks, and simple geometry. 2. Build a CSS mesh/aurora with restrained grain and strong typography. 3. Build a lightweight canvas composition that pauses offscreen and respects reduced motion. 4. Create a code-native product surface or device frame using real interface content. 5. Use a typographic hero with a distinctive grid and no decorative image. The fallback must look intentional. Do not label it a placeholder or leave a gray box for later. ## 8. Delivery checks - Every asset exists at the referenced path or durable URL. - Crops work at narrow and wide layouts. - Dimensions/aspect ratio prevent layout shift. - Hero media is prioritized; noncritical media lazy-loads. - Videos are silent by default, have a poster, pause offscreen, and honor reduced motion. - Files are optimized for the rendered size. - Alt text describes meaning, not visual decoration. - Source/license or generation provenance is recorded where required. - No provider credentials, temporary job URLs, watermarks, fake logos, or accidental text artifacts ship.

# Mobile UI Patterns — Study & Build Guide Mobile UI vocabulary for native and mobile-web products: navigation models, component patterns, gestures, and per-domain screen blueprints. Use alongside `theme-derivation.md` for tokens and `motion-3d-playbook.md` for motion. HTML/Tailwind snippets illustrate structure only; translate them into real native components and platform semantics for SwiftUI, UIKit, Compose, Android Views, React Native, or Flutter. ## Contents 1. Platform doctrine 2. Navigation models 3. Core components 4. Gestures and motion 5. Domain blueprints 6. Mobile quality gate --- ## 0. Platform doctrine (never mix blindly) | Concern | iOS (HIG) | Android (Material 3) | |---|---|---| | Nav bar | Bottom tab bar, 49pt, blur material | Navigation bar, 80dp, tonal surface | | Back affordance | Top-left chevron + swipe-from-left-edge | System back button/gesture | | Corners | Continuous (squircle), 10–39px radii | Shape scale 4–28dp | | Primary buttons | Rounded rect or capsule, tinted | Filled / tonal pill, state layers | | Sheets | Detents (medium/large), grabber | Modal bottom sheet, drag handle | | Typography | SF Pro — 17pt body, semibold nav titles | Roboto/M3 type scale | | Haptics | Impact/notification feedback per action | Vibration effects, subtler | Choose the target platform's doctrine for native work. For cross-platform products, define a shared brand layer while preserving each platform's navigation, back behavior, accessibility, and input expectations. Do not mix platform conventions solely for visual novelty. **Safe areas:** always pad with `env(safe-area-inset-*)`. Tab bar: `padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`. Status bar overlays: `padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top)`. **Touch targets:** ≥44×44px. Primary CTA height 48–56px. One-thumb reach: put primary actions in the bottom 60% of the screen. --- ## 1. Navigation models (pick ONE primary) ### 1.1 Bottom tab bar — the default 3–5 tabs. Active tab: accent icon + label; inactive: muted. Center tab can be a raised FAB (camera/compose). ```html
Home
``` ### 1.2 Top segmented control For 2–4 sibling views (Feed/Discover, Daily/Weekly). Pill track, sliding indicator (layoutId in Framer Motion; CSS `transform` transition in vanilla). ### 1.3 Stack navigation + large title iOS pattern: nav title starts 34pt bold inline with content, collapses to centered 17pt semibold on scroll. Implement with a scroll listener toggling two headers. ### 1.4 Drawer / side rail Only for 6+ sections or enterprise tools. On mobile-web: slide-over panel with scrim, `translateX` animation, focus-trapped. ### 1.5 Gesture-first (no visible chrome) Stories/swipe decks (card decks, short-video feeds). Always include a first-run hint (coach mark) and an escape button. --- ## 2. Core component patterns ### Sheets & modals - **Bottom sheet** (default modal on mobile): slides up, scrim 40% black, drag-to-dismiss, detents 40%/90%, 28px top radius. - **Action sheet**: list of destructive/neutral actions + separated Cancel. - **Full-screen modal**: only for focused creation (compose, checkout) — X top-left, primary action top-right or sticky bottom. ```html
``` ### Lists & cards - **Inset grouped list** (settings): rounded-16 sections on `bg-bg`, rows 44–56px, chevron right, separators inset 16px. - **Feed card**: image 4:3 or 16:9 rounded-20, title 17px semibold, meta row muted 13px, icon action row. - **Horizontal rail**: snap-scroll (`snap-x snap-mandatory`), card width 75–85% so the next card peeks. Peek = affordance. ### Inputs & forms - One field per row, 16px text (prevents iOS zoom), input height 48–52px. - Sticky bottom primary CTA above keyboard. - OTP: 4–6 segmented boxes, auto-advance, paste fill. - Toggles: iOS-style switch (accent when on), 51×31px pill. ### Feedback - **Toast/snackbar**: bottom, above tab bar, auto-dismiss 3s, one action max. - **Skeletons over spinners**: shimmer blocks matching the final layout for any load >300ms. - **Empty states**: icon/illustration 80px, one-line headline, one-line sub, one CTA. Never a bare "No data". - **Pull-to-refresh**: spinner synced to drag distance. --- ## 3. Gesture & motion vocabulary (mobile) | Gesture | Use | Motion | |---|---|---| | Tap | all actions | scale 0.97, 120ms | | Long-press | context menu / preview | haptic + scale-in menu from touch point | | Swipe horizontal | card deck, tab change, list actions | follow finger, spring release | | Swipe down | dismiss sheet/photo, refresh | translateY follows finger, scrim fades | | Pinch | photo/map zoom | transform scale, clamp 0.5–3× | | Edge swipe (left) | back | interactive pop transition | Mobile hero motion: entrance stagger (eyebrow → headline → sub → CTA → visual, 80ms steps), hero visual floats on a 4px y-loop, scroll parallax on decorative blobs only. 3D scroll effects from `motion-3d-playbook.md` apply on mobile too, but clamp `translateZ` depths ≤60px and never scroll-jack on touch — use native vertical scroll with parallax layers instead. --- ## 4. Domain screen blueprints (the full idea catalog) Each entry: structure + the ONE thing that makes it award-level. ### 4.1 Onboarding / auth Splash → 3–5 swipeable value slides (illustration + headline + page dots) → sign-up (social first, email last) → OTP → permission priming (explain WHY before the system prompt). Award-level: illustration morphs between slides; progress dot expands into a pill. ### 4.2 Social / feed Stories rail (rings for unseen) → infinite feed cards → FAB compose → detail with shared-element transition from the card. Award-level: shared-element hero image + like-button particle burst. ### 4.3 Finance / wallet Balance hero (huge mono number, sparkline) → quick actions row (send/request/scan/top-up as circular icon buttons) → transactions grouped by day with category chips → card screen with a 3D-tilting card. Award-level: balance counts up on load; amounts blur until tapped (privacy toggle). ### 4.4 Health / fitness / yoga Daily ring/progress hero → today's plan as timeline cards → session player (full-bleed video, big timer, minimal chrome) → weekly bar stats. Award-level: breathing-animation circle; rings draw on via stroke-dashoffset. ### 4.5 Food / delivery Sticky search + location header → category chip rail → hero dish carousel (snap) → restaurant cards (image, rating pill, ETA) → dish detail with parallax header that shrinks into the navbar → cart sheet with steppers → live order tracking. Award-level: add-to-cart flies the item into the cart icon. ### 4.6 E-commerce / product 2-col product grid (image 1:1, bold price, wishlist heart) → product page: gallery pager → title/price → color/size chips → sticky bottom "Add to bag" → cart → single-column checkout. Award-level: pointer-tilt product hero; size-chip selection springs. ### 4.7 Smart home / IoT dashboard Room selector chips → device grid cards (icon + name + state + inline toggle) → device detail: BIG radial/slider control center-stage → scenes row. Award-level: draggable radial thermostat dial with haptic ticks; active device cards glow in accent (neumorphic or glass — pick per theme). ### 4.8 Chat / messaging Conversation list (avatar, name, last message, time, unread badge) → thread: grouped bubbles, day separators, sticky input bar → media viewer with pinch-zoom + swipe-down dismiss. Award-level: message send morphs from the input; typing indicator with bouncing dots. ### 4.9 Music / media player Library lists → now-playing: blurred album-art background, big art rounded-24, scrubber, controls (72px play), lyrics sheet. Award-level: background hue extracted from the art; mini-player expands with shared-element. ### 4.10 Reading / novel / docs Cover grid → reader: serif 19px, line-height 1.7, tap zones (prev/next/menu), chapter sheet, theme presets (paper/sepia/dark), hairline progress bar. Award-level: ambient theme that shifts with time of day. ### 4.11 Game UI Hex/tile grids, HUD overlays (health, resources in top corners), bottom ability bar with radial cooldown sweeps. Award-level: floating damage numbers with physics; cooldown sweep via conic-gradient mask. ### 4.12 AI chat / agent console Thread list → chat: user right-bubbles, agent left with avatar, streaming text reveal, tool-call cards (collapsible, status → result), code blocks with copy, sticky composer with model-picker chip. Award-level: "thinking" shimmer state; tool cards expand inline with spring; text streams in word-by-word. ### 4.13 Profile / settings Header (avatar 88px, name, handle, edit) → stats row → content tabs or inset grouped list. Settings: destructive actions separated in red, version line in footer. Award-level: stretchy header — avatar parallax-zooms on pull-down. --- ## 5. Mobile quality gate (in addition to SKILL.md Phase 5) 1. Safe-area insets on ALL fixed chrome (tab bar, sheets, sticky CTAs). 2. Every interactive element ≥44px; primary CTA reachable one-handed. 3. Text inputs ≥16px font (no iOS auto-zoom). 4. Sheets dismiss by drag AND scrim tap AND back button. 5. Skeletons for all async content; optimistic UI for likes/sends/toggles. 6. Horizontal rails always show a peek of the next item. 7. No scroll-jacking on touch; parallax depth ≤60px; everything honors `prefers-reduced-motion`. 8. Test a small and large supported device class, landscape where relevant, and increased text size. For mobile web, include 375×667 and 430×932. Content must never hide behind the tab bar; reserve its height plus the safe area. 9. Native work uses platform semantics, Dynamic Type/font scaling, screen-reader labels, and system Reduce Motion settings—not DOM-only attributes or CSS assumptions.

# Dashboard system

Design dashboards as decision systems, not collections of attractive cards.

## Contents

1. Question hierarchy
2. Shell and grid
3. Metric grammar
4. Visualization selection
5. Tables and filters
6. Operational states
7. Compact telemetry

## 1. Question hierarchy

For every dashboard, write the three to seven questions it must answer in priority order. Map each question to one primary component and define the action enabled by the answer. Remove components that do not support a question, decision or necessary context.

Separate:

- **monitoring:** What needs attention now?
- **analysis:** Why did it happen?
- **planning:** What is likely next?
- **execution:** What can the user do?

Do not make one screen equally responsible for all four modes without progressive disclosure.

## 2. Shell and grid

- Keep global navigation, workspace/account context and global filters visually distinct from page-local controls.
- Use a 12-column desktop grid or an equivalent explicit layout system; spans reflect information importance.
- Align card edges, titles, values and plotting areas. Vary size deliberately, not randomly.
- Make the primary analytical region at least twice the visual weight of supporting cards.
- Preserve a stable shell when navigating between dashboard routes.
- At narrow widths, collapse navigation before compressing analytical content below its minimum contract.

## 3. Metric grammar

A trustworthy metric includes:

- value and unit;
- time window and aggregation;
- comparison baseline when change is shown;
- direction and magnitude of change;
- freshness/provenance when operationally relevant;
- target, threshold or forecast only when defined.

Use tabular numerals. Distinguish zero, unavailable, not applicable, private and not-yet-calculated values.

## 4. Visualization selection

| Question | Prefer | Avoid |
|---|---|---|
| Change over time | line/area, small multiples | donut, decorative gauge |
| Compare categories | ordered bar, dot plot, table | perspective/3D bars |
| Part-to-whole | stacked bar; donut only for few stable parts | many-slice pie |
| Distribution | histogram, box/violin when audience understands | averages alone |
| Relationship | scatter/bubble with clear encoding | dual-axis chart without justification |
| Progress to target | bullet/progress/target card | speedometer unless physical rate metaphor matters |
| Schedule/status over time | timeline/Gantt/status matrix | unrelated KPI cards |
| Geographic pattern | map plus accessible table | map when location is incidental |

Never truncate an axis to exaggerate change without making the scale unmistakable. Annotate material events and uncertainty.

## 5. Tables and filters

- Use tables for exact lookup, dense comparison and operational actions.
- Provide sorting, pagination/virtualization, column visibility and sticky context only when data scale requires them.
- Keep row actions keyboard accessible and discoverable without hover.
- Show filter scope, active count and clear/reset behavior; serialize shareable filters into URL state when appropriate.
- Preserve selection across pagination only when the action scope is explicit.
- Require confirmation and impact summary for destructive bulk actions.

## 6. Operational states

Show refresh progress without wiping usable data. Mark stale or partial sections independently. For real-time views, provide pause/follow controls and avoid shifting content under the pointer. Surface data latency and source failures close to affected elements.

## 7. Compact telemetry

For rings, gauges, sparklines, segmented meters and widget cards:

- display the exact value and unit;
- expose threshold/target meaning in text;
- label the time window;
- use a stable zero/baseline;
- keep one dominant metric;
- provide at least 160×96 CSS px for a card with label, value and micro-chart unless a platform-specific widget contract says otherwise;
- replace the visual with a value/list layout when the container becomes too narrow.

# Framework Routing — Web, Native, and Cross-Platform

Use this reference when the implementation stack is missing, mixed, or needs adaptation. Existing project architecture wins unless the user requests a change.

## Contents

1. Selection rules
2. Web routing
3. Mobile routing
4. Desktop and embedded surfaces
5. Component and state architecture
6. Dependency policy

## 1. Selection rules

1. Inspect manifests, lockfiles, route structure, style system, and component conventions.
2. Continue in the existing stack and version range.
3. Prefer native platform capabilities before adding libraries.
4. Add a dependency only when it removes meaningful risk or repeated code.
5. Keep examples in references conceptual; adapt syntax to the installed framework.

## 2. Web routing

| Context | Preferred implementation |
|---|---|
| Existing React/Next app | existing router, server/client boundary, CSS solution, and component conventions |
| Existing Vue/Nuxt app | Composition API and existing router/store/style conventions |
| Existing Svelte/SvelteKit app | existing load/actions/routing patterns and scoped styles |
| Existing Angular app | standalone/module conventions already present, Angular forms and CDK where installed |
| No-build prototype | semantic HTML, modern CSS, and small ES modules |
| Content-heavy public site | framework's static/server rendering path with progressive enhancement |
| Dashboard/product app | route-level code splitting, resilient data states, accessible component primitives |

Do not force Tailwind, React, GSAP, Lenis, Framer Motion, or Three.js into a project that does not need them. Translate the design tokens and behavior into the project's native system.

### Styling translation

- Tailwind: map semantic tokens into the existing config or CSS variables.
- CSS Modules/scoped CSS: keep tokens global and component styles local.
- CSS-in-JS: reuse the project's theme provider; avoid introducing a second theme system.
- Design-system library: extend through documented tokens/variants rather than overriding internals.
- Plain CSS: use cascade layers, custom properties, logical properties, and component classes.

## 3. Mobile routing

| Target | Implementation guidance |
|---|---|
| SwiftUI | use NavigationStack, semantic controls, Dynamic Type, safe areas, Reduce Motion, and platform materials |
| UIKit | preserve controller/navigation architecture; use Auto Layout, traits, and accessibility APIs |
| Jetpack Compose | use Material/theme primitives, navigation already installed, window insets, semantics, and motion settings |
| Android Views | preserve XML/view-binding architecture and platform accessibility behavior |
| React Native / Expo | use native navigation and gesture stack already present; avoid DOM-only assumptions |
| Flutter | use ThemeData, semantic widgets, Navigator/router already present, MediaQuery accessibility settings |
| Mobile web/PWA | use semantic HTML, safe-area env variables, touch targets, and native scrolling |

HTML/Tailwind snippets in other references describe structure, not 1:1 native code. Rebuild them with native components and platform interaction doctrine.

## 4. Desktop and embedded surfaces

- Electron/Tauri: keep the web UI accessible and avoid blocking the main process with visual work.
- Browser extensions: honor CSP, compact widths, keyboard use, and permission messaging.
- Embedded widgets: isolate styles, keep bundle size bounded, and avoid assuming full-page scroll ownership.
- TV/kiosk: use focus navigation, large targets, overscan-safe spacing, and remote/keyboard interaction.

## 5. Component and state architecture

Separate:

- semantic tokens from component implementation;
- layout shells from route content;
- presentational components from data loading;
- interaction state from animation state;
- server data, optimistic state, and error recovery;
- decorative media from task-critical information.

Build primitives only when the project lacks them. Prefer a small set of reusable components over one generated component per visual variation.

## 6. Dependency policy

Before adding a package, confirm:

- the same capability is not already present;
- its license and runtime environment fit the project;
- version compatibility with the lockfile and framework;
- server/client or native-platform constraints;
- bundle and performance cost;
- reduced-motion, keyboard, and cleanup behavior;
- a removal/fallback path.

Use CSS transitions and platform animation APIs for ordinary interactions. Use a motion library for coordinated state/route choreography. Use GSAP-like scroll tooling only for complex marketing sequences. Use WebGL only when the spatial narrative earns the cost.

# 3D Product Scrollytelling — Exploded Assemblies & Cinematic Technical Visualization

Scroll-driven product storytelling: assembled → rotate → open → explode → focus → annotate → reassemble. This chapter owns **part-level product choreography** — exploded views, disassembly, cutaways, x-ray reveals — on the premium black-background aesthetic. It builds on [threejs-scroll-world.md](threejs-scroll-world.md) (scene architecture, R3F/vanilla wiring, lifecycle) and [motion-3d-playbook.md](motion-3d-playbook.md) (Lenis + GSAP ScrollTrigger setup); read those for the how, this for the what and the rules.

Machine-readable assets: `assets/scrollytelling-recipes.json` (deterministic beat maps) and `assets/scroll-scene.js` (renderer-agnostic progress engine). Reference imagery and study links: [scrollytelling-references.md](scrollytelling-references.md).

## Contents

1. When to reach for this (and when not)
2. The primitive: scroll progress owns the scene
3. Recipe catalog
4. Beat maps
5. Rendering tiers and the never-flatten rule
6. GLB and part conventions
7. The scroll engine contract
8. UX contract (non-negotiable)
9. Performance budgets
10. Accessibility and honest duplication

## 1. When to reach for this (and when not)

Reach for it when a **physical or physically-imagined product** is the hero and its internals or construction ARE the story: hardware launches (watch, phone, GPU, drone, camera, EV component, AI chip, robot), premium DTC objects (sneaker, espresso machine), technical credibility pages ("how it's built"), and configurators that earn a narrative intro. One scrollytelling scene per page; it is the landing's "one dominant motion idea" from [landing-system.md](landing-system.md), never an addition to one.

Do **not** use it for dashboards, tools, or any surface where the person came to act rather than be told a story; where no genuine part hierarchy exists (a T-shirt is not an assembly); or where the budget only affords a flattened video — then use an ordinary media section instead of a fake-interactive one.

## 2. The primitive: scroll progress owns the scene

Normalized progress `p ∈ [0,1]` over a pinned section is the **only clock**. Every scene property — camera distance/height/orbit/fov, per-part explosion, shell opacity, clip plane, highlight, caption — is a pure function of `p`. Consequences:

- **Scrub, never play.** No timers advance the scene. Scrolling back replays backward perfectly (reversibility is free when state is a function, impossible when it's a video you fired).
- **Deterministic beats.** A recipe is a list of keyframes (`beats`) at fixed `p` values; the engine interpolates numeric fields between adjacent beats and switches discrete fields at beat boundaries.
- The scene owns real objects (Tier A) whenever possible, so `p` can drive positions, materials, lights and annotations independently — the reason this beats scrubbing a video.

## 3. Recipe catalog

Twenty deterministic recipes ship in `assets/scrollytelling-recipes.json`. Pick **one primary** per scene; a second may be nested only as a sub-beat (e.g., `component-focus` inside `exploded-assembly` — the shipped `exploded-assembly` already includes two focus beats).

| Recipe | Intent | Tiers |
|---|---|---|
| `product-reveal` | Darkness → rim light → silhouette → full product | A B C |
| `exploded-assembly` | The canonical: rotate, explode, focus ×2, reassemble | A B |
| `product-disassembly` | Parts leave one by one in service order | A B |
| `internal-reveal` | Shell fades, internals stay lit | A B |
| `layer-peel` | Concentric layers lift in sequence (shoe, battery, PCB stack) | A B |
| `component-focus` | Camera dollies to one part; rest dims; spec appears | A B |
| `xray-reveal` | Materials go translucent by scroll; skeleton/frame glows | A |
| `material-transformation` | Raw material → machined → finished surface | A B C |
| `assembly-sequence` | Parts fly in and seat (reverse disassembly) | A B |
| `floating-components` | Parts drift in loose formation; labels attach | A |
| `orbital-inspection` | 360° orbit with 3–5 annotated stations | A B |
| `camera-fly-through` | Camera travels through the open product | A |
| `mechanical-operation` | One mechanism cycles as scroll advances (gears, hinge, shutter) | A B |
| `product-morph` | Model A transitions to model B (generations, sizes) | A |
| `cutaway-reveal` | Clip plane sweeps a cross-section | A |
| `particle-assembly` | Product condenses from particles, then solidifies | A |
| `technical-blueprint` | Wireframe/blueprint style resolves into rendered product | A |
| `reassembly-hero` | Exploded start; scroll assembles toward CTA | A B |
| `macro-zoom` | Extreme close-up travels the surface to a wide hero | A B C |
| `hero-to-grid` | Hero product recedes into a comparison/spec grid handoff | A B |

## 4. Beat maps

A beat map is the recipe's spine. Format (see the JSON for full schema):

```json
{ "p": 0.42, "label": "internals-emerge",
  "state": { "rotY": 0.35, "explode": 0.7, "shellFade": 0.85,
             "focus": -1, "camDist": 3.2, "camHeight": 0.4, "fov": 40 },
  "caption": "flight-controller" }
```

Worked ledger for `exploded-assembly` (the shipped default):

```
p 0.00  black; rim light only            0.52  full exploded state
  0.06  silhouette resolves              0.62  camera approaches board
  0.12  key light up, product assembled  0.70  board highlighted + spec caption
  0.20  slow quarter turn                0.78  second focus: battery + caption
  0.30  shell separates                  0.86  components return
  0.42  internals emerge                 0.95  reassembled, settle turn
                                         1.00  CTA handoff
```

Rules: beats are monotonic in `p`; first beat at 0 and last at 1; **something must visibly change within the first 0.05** (immediate feedback); captions attach to beats, and every caption's content also exists in the plain-DOM narrative (§10).

## 5. Rendering tiers and the never-flatten rule

**Tier A — real-time 3D (default).** GLB/glTF parts → Three.js or R3F; `p` drives transforms, materials, lights. Choose whenever a part hierarchy exists or can be modeled.
**Tier B — rendered frame sequence.** Blender/C4D render → WebP/AVIF frames → canvas scrub (the Apple AirPods technique). Choose for photoreal scenes too heavy for live rendering. Frames are still driven by the same beat map (`frame = round(p × (N−1))`); captions and landmarks stay real DOM.
**Tier C — video scrub.** `video.currentTime = p × duration`. Last resort only: seeking is imprecise and keyframe-dependent, reversal stutters, parts can't be addressed. Requires an all-keyframe (I-frame) encode.

**The asset rule: never flatten a usable multipart 3D product into video if the component hierarchy can be preserved.** A watch, phone, GPU, server, engine, drone, sneaker or robot with separable parts becomes an interactive scroll narrative (Tier A), not decorative footage. Downgrade tiers only for photorealism the GPU budget can't carry (→ B) or when the source simply isn't reconstructable (→ C).

## 6. GLB and part conventions

- **Hierarchy**: one root `product`; direct children are addressable parts named `part_<slug>` in disassembly order (`part_glass`, `part_screen`, `part_board`, `part_battery`, `part_shell_back`). Sub-assemblies nest one level max.
- **Pivots** sit at each part's *assembled* position; explosion is a translation from rest, so `explode = 0` is always exactly the assembled product.
- **Explosion vectors** live in a JSON sidecar (or glTF `extras`): `{ "part_glass": { "dir": [0,1,0], "dist": 1.2, "order": 1 } }` — per-part direction (unit), distance (in product-radius units), and stagger order. Configurable per component, ExplodeView-style.
- **Scale/units**: meters; product normalized so its bounding radius ≈ 1 — camera distances in recipes are multiples of it.
- **Compression**: Draco or Meshopt; textures KTX2 (fallback WebP) ≤ 2048px; PBR with one material per part so dim/highlight is a per-part `opacity`/`emissive` write, never a shared-material mutation.
- Author the black-background look in the scene (rim + key lights, dark env), not baked into textures, so packs can retint via `--ifx-grad-a/b` accent lights.

## 7. The scroll engine contract

`assets/scroll-scene.js` (`window.IFXScrollScene`) is dependency-free and renderer-agnostic — it computes progress and interpolated beat state; Three.js, canvas-sequence or video adapters consume it. GSAP ScrollTrigger can replace it 1:1 where already present (map `self.progress` to the same beat interpolation).

```js
const scene = IFXScrollScene.create({
  section: document.querySelector('#story'),   // tall pinned section
  beats: recipes['exploded-assembly'].beats,
  onUpdate(state, p, info) { /* write state.* into your renderer */ },
  onBeat(beat, dir) { /* captions, landmarks, aria-live */ },
});
```

Guarantees: passive listeners only (never preventDefault — no scroll hijacking); rAF-coalesced updates only while the section intersects; numeric fields eased between beats, discrete fields switched at beats; `prefers-reduced-motion` detected and (by default) progress quantized to beat states — stepped, still reversible; `destroy()` releases everything. Helpers: `lerp, remap, clamp, ease.*`.

## 8. UX contract (non-negotiable)

Field feedback on scroll-driven 3D sites is consistent: people abandon when scrolling feels dead and get disoriented when reversing misbehaves. Every scrollytelling scene therefore ships with:

1. **Immediate feedback** — visible change within the first 5% of the pin; never a long dead zone before the scene "starts".
2. **Reversible timeline** — scrolling up exactly rewinds; no one-way triggers, no re-fired entrance animations.
3. **Landmarks** — a progress rail with labeled beat dots that are real buttons (scroll-to on activation); current beat reflected in text.
4. **No scroll hijacking** — native scroll + `position: sticky`; wheel/touch are never captured or re-timed. (Smoothing via Lenis is acceptable; capturing is not.)
5. **Honest pin length** — 300–600vh desktop; more scroll than story is padding, less is whiplash.
6. **Reduced motion** — stepped beat states or a static poster + the full text narrative; parallax and particle drift removed.
7. **Mobile simplification** — pin ≤ 350vh, DPR ≤ 1.5, part count and lights reduced, captions become an inline stack; touch never fights vertical scroll.
8. **Escape hatch** — content after the pin is reachable by keyboard and a "skip story" link precedes the scene.

## 9. Performance budgets

Hero scene ≤ 150k triangles, ≤ 80 draw calls, textures ≤ 2048 KTX2/WebP, total 3D payload ≤ 6 MB (Tier B: frames ≤ 4 MB via AVIF/WebP ~85% quality, ≤ 160 frames, resolution-switched by viewport). Lazy-init on approach (IntersectionObserver, one viewport early); pause rendering when off-screen; cap `devicePixelRatio` at 2 (1.5 mobile); scene update ≤ 8 ms on a mid-tier phone. Preload strategy for Tier B: first + last frames immediately, the rest in idle time, decode ahead of the scrub direction.

## 10. Accessibility and honest duplication

The canvas is `aria-hidden`; the story exists in parallel as ordinary DOM: headings per act, the same captions and spec values in a plain section after the pin (the "spec sheet" duplicates every annotated number). Beat changes may announce politely (throttled) via a visually-hidden live region. Focus order ignores the scene entirely; the progress-rail buttons are the only interactive scene chrome. If WebGL is unavailable, render the poster + narrative — the page must still sell the product with zero JavaScript-driven motion.

Reference translation law applies here as everywhere: study the linked material for **beat timing, camera language, lighting-on-black, part choreography and annotation style** — never copy a specific product's model, footage, or composition.

# Page Templates — Complete Multi-Page Delivery Contract

Use this reference when the user asks for a full UI, complete pages, a whole template, or a clearly multi-route product. Deliver the requested route set and all states reachable from the promised primary flows. Do not force this matrix onto a single-page request or invent legal/product copy the user did not authorize.

---

## 1. Completeness rules

1. **Every nav item and CTA on a page must resolve to a real page/state.** Dead links and `#` hrefs are a defect. In static previews, use hash routing or in-app navigation so every route works.
2. **Minimum complete set:** the requested primary routes + every destination exposed by their navigation + auth when accounts are in scope + applicable not-found/empty/error states.
3. **Shared chrome is identical across pages:** same navbar, footer, tokens, motion system. Extract it once, reuse everywhere.
4. **Each page still gets ONE dominant element** and the full Phase 2 theme — secondary pages are not excuses for plain design.
5. **States, not just screens:** every list/table ships with loading skeleton, empty state, and error state; every form ships with validation + success feedback.

## 2. Page-set matrix (pick the product row, build ALL its pages)

| Product | Required pages |
|---|---|
| Marketing / landing site | Home plus the feature, pricing, story, content, contact, and legal routes explicitly present in the brief/navigation · 404 |
| SaaS app | Landing · Login · Signup · Forgot password · Onboarding wizard · Dashboard home · Core feature pages (2–4) · Settings (profile/billing/notifications) · Empty + error states |
| Mobile app UI | Onboarding (3–5 slides) · Login/OTP · Home tab · 2–4 remaining tabs · Key detail screen · Sheet/modal flows · Profile/settings — per `mobile-ui-patterns.md` |
| E-commerce | Home · Category/grid · Product detail · Cart · Checkout (address → payment → confirm) · Order success · Account/orders · 404 |
| Dashboard / admin / AI console | Login · Overview (KPIs + charts) · Data table page (filter/sort/paginate) · Detail/entity page · Live activity or console feed · Settings · Empty/error states |
| Portfolio | Home · Work index · Case-study detail · About · Contact · 404 |
| Docs / knowledge base | Docs home (search hero) · Article page (sidebar TOC, prev/next) · Changelog · 404 |

## 3. Secondary page skeletons

### 3.1 Pricing
Eyebrow + headline → billing toggle (monthly/yearly, yearly shows "save 20%") → 3 tier cards (middle elevated: accent border, scale-105, "Most popular" pill) → feature checklist rows with ✓ → FAQ accordion → final CTA band. Award-level: toggle animates prices counting; recommended card has slow ambient glow.

### 3.2 Auth (login / signup / forgot)
Split layout: left = form card (logo, headline "Welcome back", social buttons → divider → email/password → submit → footer link swap login/signup), right = brand panel with product visual or animated gradient. Mobile: form only, brand panel becomes a compact header. Award-level: inputs float labels; submit button morphs to spinner → success check → redirect.

### 3.3 Onboarding wizard (app setup)
3–5 steps, top progress bar or dots, one question per screen, big selectable cards/chips, Back ghost + Continue primary (disabled until valid), final "All set" celebration (confetti or scale-in check). Skippable.

### 3.4 Settings
Sidebar section list (desktop) / inset grouped list (mobile) → panels: Profile (avatar upload, fields), Account (email, password, delete — danger zone separated, red), Notifications (toggle rows), Billing (plan card + invoices table), API/Integrations (key rows with copy + reveal). Award-level: unsaved-changes bar slides up ("Save / Discard").

### 3.5 Data table page
Header (title + primary action "New X") → toolbar (search, filter chips, sort, column toggle) → table (sticky header, row hover, status pill cells, row actions ⋮) → pagination or infinite scroll. States: skeleton rows, empty ("No X yet" + CTA), error banner with retry.

### 3.6 Detail / entity page
Breadcrumb → title row (name + status pill + actions) → stat cards row → tabbed body (Overview / Activity / Settings) → right rail (meta, assignees, timestamps) on desktop, stacked on mobile.

### 3.7 Blog index + post
Index: featured post card (large) + grid of cards (image 16:9, tag chip, title, date · read time). Post: centered 680–720px column, H1 + meta row, hero image, prose styles (h2 anchors, code blocks, pull quotes), author card, prev/next. Award-level: reading-progress hairline bar; headings reveal on scroll.

### 3.8 Contact / about
Contact: split — left headline + channels (email, socials, office), right form card (name/email/message) with inline validation + success state replacing the form. About: story timeline, values grid, team cards with hover photo treatment, stats band.

### 3.9 404 / empty / error
404: oversized display numeral (dominant element), one-line wit, "Back home" primary + search or popular links. Empty: icon 80px + headline + sub + CTA. Error: banner or full-page with retry button and reference ID.

### 3.10 Checkout (3 steps, single column)
Step indicator (1 Address → 2 Payment → 3 Review) → forms with validation → order summary card sticky right (desktop) / collapsible top (mobile) → success page: big animated check, order number, "Track order" + "Continue shopping".

## 4. Navigation between pages

- **React (webapp-building):** routes wired in App.tsx with the provided router — every page is a real component in `src/pages/`.
- **Vanilla HTML:** one folder, `index.html` links to sibling pages (`pricing.html`, …); identical header/footer markup on each; motion via `assets/motion-utils.js` auto-init.
- **Mobile shell:** bottom tab bar on every tab page; detail pages push over with back chevron (see `mobile-ui-patterns.md` §1.3).

## 5. Handoff checklist for "complete template" deliveries

1. Every route in the nav/footer/CTAs renders real content.
2. Shared chrome consistent; tokens identical on all pages.
3. Loading / empty / error states present on data pages.
4. 3D scroll layer on the primary page (unless opted out), lighter motion on utility pages (auth/settings get entrance transitions only).
5. All pages pass the Phase 5 quality gate + responsive check at 375px and 1440px.
